reports.desc: They call repeatedly from 1-540-385-0941, leaving a voicemail to call them back at 775-438-1723. I called them and told them to stop calling my number and remove it from the database, that I owe zero taxes then she proceeded to ask me if I had received a letter saying that I owed taxes , with a heavy accent. I told her I owed zero money to remove my number again -and she hung up on me. I couldn’t get anyone to answer on the 530 number. Total scammers trying to act like they are a tax service, to help people that owe money to the American IRS. I hope they all get arrested. I’d report it to the FBI if I knew how but I’m sure they’ve got bigger fish to fry. Block them or hide your number and spam call them back, if you know how to do that. Tired of daily voicemails from scammers . They generally don’t answer when you try to call them back.

Ordered Akemi in May(3 months supply). They sent another 3 months worth in June and July, almost another 3 in August.  I only ordered in May. Called to cancel and get a refund. Took almost an hour to convince to stop the orders and they told me no refund, would give discount on further order. Tried EMAIL as well, they wont return EMAILS.

The site presented itself as the central website for a popular brand of protein shakes and is visually almost identical to the actual website of this company. When I attempted to pay, luckily, the verification code didn't send to my phone number and after a couple of tries, I got suspicious of the site and realized it was a a fake. However, I have since had multiple attemtps to access my banking information, though the two-factor authentification has not been breached.

I paid for and supposedly took an IQ test. I was charged $1.95 through PayPal. Today, August 27, 2027 I received a PayPal notice authorizing $39.95 For Nordica lab. I did not authorize any additional payments to Nordicsl lab. In fact test was incorrect. I do not want to pay Nordica lab any further amount. I paid the initial amount as requested for the supposed results.
I have contacted PayPal to deny amount but now have opened a case. What else do I need to do?

An ad pops up on social media advertising a book of old remedies. When you purchase the book, you are unwittingly signed up for a subscription. I purchased the book on August 20, and I was charged $49 on August 27. I had no idea why I was being charged. After doing some research, including looking on the Better Business Bureau's website, I saw that other people had also reported that they had no idea they had subscribed to anything. I also found out that although their website shows a Tennessee address, but they are actually a Lithuanian company. Beware of Old Ways Remedies which is owned by Herbal Solutions UAB out of Lithuania.
